sentences.text:
The gravamen of indictment against the applicant is that t  SSP 1/4  ::: Uploaded on - 17/04/2024 ::: Downloaded on  907 ABA 910 OF 2024.
and Manilal Dedhia, who represented Rajshree Constructions, Builders and Developers, induced the first informant and his associates to part with huge amount of Rs.1,72,50,000/- by making a false representation that the first informant and the associates would be allotted flats on 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th floors of the building Mitra Tower, which they professed to develop.
The applicant had issued allotment letters in the year 2010.
However, no development could be carried out till the year 2024.
Hence, the first informant lodged the report.
8. Learned Counsel for the Applicant submits that the first informant and the other investors claimed to have paid an exorbitant amount to the applicant.

In fact,
the allotment letters record the amount which was paid by way of earnest by each of the investors.
The applicant is willing to repay the said amounts along with the compensation for having utilized the said amounts for all these years.
It was further submitted that there is an inordinate delay in lodging the report.

9. Learned Counsel for the applicant, on instructions, submits that the applicant is willing to deposit the amounts which the applicant has received by cheques from the 18 flat purchasers within two months.
10. Learned APP resisted the prayer for bail.
It was submitted that as many as 9 persons have been duped to the tune of Rs.1,72,50,000/- The applicant has induced the unsuspecting flat purchasers to part with their hard earn money.
Therefore, the applicant does not deserve pre-arrest bail.

sentences.text: I have perused the allegations in the FIR and the documents.
Prima facie, it appears that while the allotment letters were issued, the parties had fixed th consideration to be paid, as also the earnest money which was parted with by the flat purchasers.

The amount which the first informant and rest of investors / flat purchasers claimed to have parted with, appears to be substantially higher then the amount which finds mention in the allotment letters.
There is an element of delay in lodging the FIR as the allotment letters were issued in the year 2010.
12. In these circumstances, it may be expedient to protect the liberty of th applicant while directing the applicant to cooperate with the investigation.

It may also be expedient to implead the first informant as party Respondent No.2 to this Application and, thereafter, decide the application after providing an effective opportunity of hearing to the first informant/investors and prosecution.

13. Hence, the following order :
 ORDER (i) In the event of the arrest of the Applicant - Raju Bhojraj Advani in connection with C.R.No.48 of 2024 registered with Chunabhatti Police Station, the Applicant be released on bail on furnishing a PR bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- with one or two sureties in the like amount.

(ii) The Applicant shall co-operate with the investigation and report to Chunabhatti Police Station on 22nd, 23rd and 24th April 2024 between 10.00 a.m. to 907 ABA 910 OF 2024.doc 1.00 p.m.,
and, thereafter, as and when directed.

(iii) The Applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence and/or give threat or inducement to the first informant or any of the prosecution witnesses or any of the persons acquainted with the facts of the case.
(iv) The Applicant shall deposit the amounts, as undertaken, in this Court on or before 14 June 2024.
(v) Stand over to 18 June 2024.
